# Part 2: Power and sample size calculations

In this part, we use computer generated data to better understand the concepts type I error, power and sample size calculations To generate data, a random number generator is used. To make such calculations reproducible, a seed is provided to the random number generator. In R, function `set.seed` allows to set the seed for all ensuing random numbers being generated. If you want to compare results exactly with the solutions, use the following seed:

```{r}
  # set a seed to make the markdown file reproducible
  set.seed(-1354273014)
```

**Note**: Your results will only be identical, if all random numbers are generated in the same order and amount.

In general, it is good practice to derive the seed itself from a "random" source, such as using the current time `as.integer(Sys.time())`. Generating and analyzing random data repeatedly is called data simulation.


## Generate random data

Generate two data sets of sample size `N <- 100` using function `rnorm` as follows:

```{r}
  X <- rnorm(N, 0, 1.5)
  Y <- rnorm(N, 0, 1.5)
```
In this case, both data sets have sample size `N`, mean 0 and standard deviation 1.5.

Compare the data sets using a t-test. What is the p-value?

## Simulations

Power and type-I error are probabilites about the study outcome. With synthetic data, we can repeat the study many times and thus directly calculate type-I error from results attained in the computer. The following code repeats the calculations above many times using a 'for' loop.

```{r}
Nrepetitions <- 5000
p.values = NULL
for (i in 1:Nrepetitions) {
  X <- rnorm(N, 0, 1.5)
  Y <- rnorm(N, 0, 1.5)
  tt <- t.test(X, Y)
  p.values[i] <- tt$p.value
}
```
After running the code, the vector 'p.values' contains the P-values of the `Nrepetion` studies performed in the simulation.

We set our alpha level (same as type-I eror) to 0.05.

How can you calculate the type-I error in the simulation from these P-values? Describe the calculation in words. What do you expect? Perform the calculation in R.
